lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: variability and overlap

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A data set is: 17, 25, 16, 22, with a mean of 20. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?

steps: Find each value's distance from the mean: |17-20| = 3, |25-20| = 5, |16-20| = 4, |22-20| = 2.
Divide by the number of values: 14 ÷ 4 = 3 1/2.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Two data sets have means of 43 and 56. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 7. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
Sample A: 45, 35, 40, 46, 29. Sample B: 53, 47, 49, 54, 67. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample B, with a mean of 54 compared to 39.
Sample B, with a mean of 39 compared to 54.
Both samples have the same mean.
Sample A, with a mean of 39 compared to 54.

items.prompt: Sample A: 52, 17, 48, 32, 53, 53. Sample B: 35, 39, 39, 36, 38, 37. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample A, with a range of 36 compared to 4.
Both samples have the same range.
Sample B, with a range of 4 compared to 36.
Sample B, with a range of 36 compared to 4.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 891 visitors to a science museum. She randomly selects 119 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A student surveys the 74 commuters on a train line sitting closest to her. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 31 shoppers at a grocery store, 11 preferred an extended weekend event. Based on this sample, about how many of the 124 shoppers at a grocery store would you expect to prefer an extended weekend event?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
